title: Cable Schedules & Termination Drawings
objective: Develop the ability to create and review cable schedules and termination information as controlled design records, with traceability from source equipment through destination, cable identification, termination and drawing references.

learn.heading: What senior designers should understand
bullets: A cable schedule is a controlled coordination record: every cable should be traceable to its source, destination, function and associated drawings.
Cable identifiers, core information, sizes, types, lengths and termination details must be consistent with the design basis and related documents.
Do not invent missing data. Distinguish confirmed information, design assumptions and information requiring clarification.
Termination drawings should make the physical and functional interface clear enough for drafting, checking, installation and commissioning teams to understand the intended connection.
Cross-check schedules against SLDs, equipment lists, panel schedules and I/O or instrumentation information before issue.
learn.takeaway: Senior ownership means maintaining traceability across documents and identifying discrepancies before they become construction or commissioning problems.

apply.scenario: You are given a fictional pump-station package containing a motor control panel, two pumps, local isolators and several control interfaces. The source information is incomplete and contains two intentional tag mismatches.
tasks: Create a small cable schedule with at least eight fictional cables covering power, control and indication circuits.
For each cable, identify source, destination, cable tag, service, core requirement and related drawing/reference.
Flag the two intentional tag mismatches and document what source information should be checked before correction.
Create a termination checklist covering cable identification, core numbering, gland/termination information and drawing cross-references.
Record at least three assumptions or missing inputs and classify each as acceptable for drafting, requiring clarification, or blocking issue.
apply.deliverable: A sanitized cable schedule plus termination/checking checklist and a short discrepancy register. Spreadsheet, table or drawing extract is acceptable.

questions.q: A cable tag in the equipment list conflicts with the SLD. What is the strongest senior response?
a: Choose whichever tag is easier to draft and continue.
Record the discrepancy, trace both sources, identify the controlled source or obtain clarification before issuing the affected information.
Delete the cable from the schedule until somebody notices it.
questions.why: A discrepancy should be traceable and resolved against the appropriate controlled source rather than silently corrected.

questions.q: Which combination gives the strongest cable traceability?
a: Source, destination, cable tag, service and linked drawing/reference information.
Cable colour and approximate length only.
questions.why: Traceability requires enough information to connect the cable record to the physical and functional design.

questions.q: An important termination detail is missing from the supplied information. What should you do?
a: Invent a likely value so the schedule looks complete.
Leave it undocumented because termination is outside drafting.
Identify the missing input, state its impact and obtain the required information before the affected deliverable is issued.
questions.why: Senior work makes uncertainty visible and manages the interface instead of hiding it.

questions.q: Which QA check is most valuable before issuing a cable schedule?
a: Check only that every row has a cable number.
Cross-check schedule records against SLDs, equipment/panel information and related termination or I/O documentation.
Sort the rows alphabetically and assume the schedule is correct.
questions.why: Cross-document consistency catches errors that a format-only check cannot detect.

check.passRule: A learner should be able to explain the reasoning behind each selected answer, not merely obtain a score.

evidence.prompt: Capture a sanitized cable schedule, termination checklist or discrepancy register that demonstrates controlled documentation and traceability.
criteria: The artefact is identifiable and sanitized.
Assumptions and missing inputs are visible.
At least one cross-document QA check is documented.
The learner explains what their evidence proves and how it was checked.

integration.home: After completion, recommend Week 6 as the next best action and show cable documentation as a recent learning milestone.
integration.journal: Prompt reflection on traceability, discrepancy handling and confidence in controlling incomplete information.
integration.portfolio: Allow the evidence record to appear as a cable documentation competency item.
